message.content:
You are verifying a Rust port against a C++ reference binary.

REFERENCE (C++):  /workspace/dataset/test4_executable
PORT (Rust):      /output/test4          <- built from /output/test4.rs
Cargo project:    /output  (also builds via `cd /output && cargo build --release` -> /output/target/release/test4)

Both take one optional positional argument (a domain string; default "example.com") and print 4 lines of "1"/"0":
  is_valid_domain, is_valid_label, is_ascii_domain, is_idn_domain

Outputs must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical. Compare with od/xxd, not with naked `echo`, so trailing-newline and CR differences cannot hide. A robust comparator:

  cmp_one() {
    local a b
    a=$(/workspace/dataset/test4_executable "$@" 2>/dev/null | od -An -c); b=$(/output/test4 "$@" 2>/dev/null | od -An -c)
    [ "$a" == "$b" ] || { printf 'MISMATCH args=%q cpp=<%s> rs=<%s>\n' "$*" "$a" "$b"; return 1; }
  }

Also compare EXIT CODES and confirm stderr is empty for both.

ENVIRONMENT: python3/python are NOT installed. Use bash loops, printf, od, tr, head, seq, awk. rustc/cargo ARE available if you want to write a generator. For arbitrary bytes use printf '\xNN' or bash $'...' quoting.
CAUTION: `s=$(printf '\x0a')` silently strips the trailing newline — command substitution eats trailing newlines. Use $'\n' for newline args, and be aware of this artifact before reporting a "mismatch" that is really a shell quoting bug. ALWAYS re-verify a suspected mismatch by invoking both binaries directly and eyeballing od output before you report it.

ESTABLISHED SPEC (byte-based, already confirmed by 657 passing differential cases):
  is_valid_domain(s) = 1 <= s.len_in_BYTES <= 255
  is_valid_label(s)  = 1 <= s.len_in_BYTES <= 63
  is_ascii_domain(s) = every byte <= 0x7F      (empty -> true)
  is_idn_domain(s)   = any byte  >  0x7F       (empty -> false)
  Content/structure is irrelevant: dots, hyphens, spaces, slashes, control chars are all accepted.
  Length limits count BYTES, not code points ("例" x 21 = 63 bytes -> valid label; "例" x 63 = 189 bytes -> invalid).
Your job is to find any input where the two binaries DISAGREE — including inputs that break this spec.


Strategy: RANDOM ASCII. Generate at least 800 pseudo-random ASCII strings of lengths 0..300 (use $RANDOM and printf; vary length distribution so boundaries 0,1,63,64,255,256 are hit often). Include punctuation, digits, mixed case, dots and hyphens in random positions. Run every one through the comparator.

Report casesRun honestly and list ONLY re-verified mismatches. An empty mismatches array is a perfectly good result — do not invent findings.

#!/bin/bash
# Random-ASCII differential sweep: C++ reference vs Rust port.
CPP=/workspace/dataset/test4_executable
RS=/output/test4

# Printable ASCII 0x20..0x7E, weighted toward domain-ish chars, plus control bytes.
CS=$' \t\n\r\x01\x02\x07\x0b\x0c\x1b\x7f'
CS+='!"#$%&'"'"'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@'
CS+='ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\]^_`'
CS+='abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~'
CS+='..--..--..--aaaAAA000...---'   # bias toward dots/hyphens/alnum
N=${#CS}

# Boundary lengths hit often.
BL=(0 0 1 1 2 3 4 62 63 63 64 64 65 66 127 128 129 190 253 254 255 255 256 256 257 258 299 300)
NB=${#BL[@]}

fail=0
cases=0

mkdir -p /tmp/dr
for ((i=0; i<900; i++)); do
  # length: 45% boundary set, 55% uniform 0..300
  if (( RANDOM % 100 < 45 )); then
    len=${BL[$(( RANDOM % NB ))]}
  else
    len=$(( (RANDOM * 32768 + RANDOM) % 301 ))
  fi

  s=''
  for ((j=0; j<len; j++)); do
    s+="${CS:$(( RANDOM % N )):1}"
  done

  a=$("$CPP" "$s" 2>/tmp/dr/ea; echo "rc=$?" ) ; ea=$(od -An -c </tmp/dr/ea)
  b=$("$RS"  "$s" 2>/tmp/dr/eb; echo "rc=$?" ) ; eb=$(od -An -c </tmp/dr/eb)
  # re-run through od to catch trailing-newline/CR differences
  ao=$("$CPP" "$s" 2>/dev/null | od -An -c)
  bo=$("$RS"  "$s" 2>/dev/null | od -An -c)
  cases=$((cases+1))

  if [ "$ao" != "$bo" ] || [ "$a" != "$b" ] || [ "$ea" != "$eb" ] || [ -s /tmp/dr/ea ] || [ -s /tmp/dr/eb ]; then
    fail=$((fail+1))
    printf 'MISMATCH i=%d len=%d\n  arg=%q\n  cpp=<%s> rc/out=<%s> err=<%s>\n  rs =<%s> rc/out=<%s> err=<%s>\n' \
      "$i" "$len" "$s" "$ao" "$a" "$ea" "$bo" "$b" "$eb"
    printf '%s' "$s" > "/tmp/dr/fail_$i.bin"
    (( fail > 12 )) && { echo "too many failures, stopping"; break; }
  fi
done
echo "CASES=$cases FAILURES=$fail"

#!/bin/bash
CPP=/workspace/dataset/test4_executable
RS=/output/test4
RANDOM=777
CS='!"#$%&'"'"'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\]^_`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~ ..--aA0'
N=${#CS}
fail=0; cases=0
cmp_one() {
  local a b ra rb ea eb
  a=$("$CPP" "$@" 2>/tmp/dr/e1 | od -An -c); ra=$?
  b=$("$RS"  "$@" 2>/tmp/dr/e2 | od -An -c); rb=$?
  "$CPP" "$@" >/dev/null 2>/tmp/dr/e1; ra=$?
  "$RS"  "$@" >/dev/null 2>/tmp/dr/e2; rb=$?
  ea=$(od -An -c </tmp/dr/e1); eb=$(od -An -c </tmp/dr/e2)
  cases=$((cases+1))
  if [ "$a" != "$b" ] || [ "$ra" != "$rb" ] || [ "$ea" != "$eb" ] || [ -s /tmp/dr/e1 ] || [ -s /tmp/dr/e2 ]; then
    fail=$((fail+1))
    printf 'MISMATCH args=%q\n  cpp out=<%s> rc=%d err=<%s>\n  rs  out=<%s> rc=%d err=<%s>\n' \
      "$*" "$a" "$ra" "$ea" "$b" "$rb" "$eb"
  fi
}
mkdir -p /tmp/dr

# Part A: every length 0..300 exactly, random printable content
for ((len=0; len<=300; len++)); do
  s=''
  for ((j=0; j<len; j++)); do s+="${CS:$(( RANDOM % N )):1}"; done
  cmp_one "$s"
done
echo "after A: cases=$cases fail=$fail"

# Part B: repeated-char strings at every boundary, several fill chars
for ch in a A 0 . - _ '*' ' ' '/' '~' $'\t'; do
  for len in 0 1 2 62 63 64 65 126 127 128 190 253 254 255 256 257 300; do
    s=''
    for ((j=0; j<len; j++)); do s+="$ch"; done
    cmp_one "$s"
  done
done
echo "after B: cases=$cases fail=$fail"

# Part C: flag-looking and structural ASCII args
for s in '-' '--' '-a' '-h' '--help' '--version' '-V' '-1' '--' '---' '-.' '.' '..' '...' \
         'a.' '.a' 'a..b' '-a.com' 'a-.com' 'a_b.com' 'a b.com' 'a/b.com' '*.com' \
         'example.com' 'EXAMPLE.COM' 'xn--fsq.com' '0' '00' 'localhost' \
         '--domain=example.com' '=x' '+x' '%s' '%n' '%%' '$PATH' '`id`' '$(id)' \
         'a
b' 'a	b' 'a\b' 'a"b' "a'b"; do
  cmp_one "$s"
done
echo "after C: cases=$cases fail=$fail"

# Part D: extra args beyond the first (should be ignored identically)
cmp_one 'example.com' 'second' 'third'
cmp_one '' 'ignored'
cmp_one 'a' '-h'
echo "CASES=$cases FAILURES=$fail"

content.text: Random-ASCII sweep complete across three independent batches plus targeted boundary/structural cases. No divergence found.

input.strategy:
RANDOM ASCII differential fuzzing. Three independent batches, all compared via `od -An -c` on stdout (never naked echo), plus exit-code and stderr-emptiness comparison on every case.

Harnesses: /tmp/rand_ascii.sh, /tmp/rand2.sh (same generator, RANDOM reseeded to 24681), /tmp/rand3.sh.

Batch 1 + 2 (900 cases each, 1800 total): pseudo-random strings built char-by-char with $RANDOM from a charset covering printable ASCII 0x20-0x7E in full (digits, mixed case, all punctuation, space) plus control bytes (\t \n \r \x01 \x02 \x07 \x0b \x0c \x1b \x7f), with the charset deliberately biased toward dots, hyphens and alnum so domain-shaped inputs occur at random positions. Length distribution mixed: 45% drawn from a boundary-weighted table {0,1,2,3,4,62,63,64,65,66,127,128,129,190,253,254,255,256,257,258,299,300} so 0/1/63/64/255/256 are hit repeatedly, 55% uniform over 0..300.

Batch 3 (534 cases):
  A. Every length 0..300 exactly once (301 cases) with random printable content — guarantees each boundary is crossed with non-degenerate content.
  B. Repeated-char strings at boundaries {0,1,2,62,63,64,65,126,127,128,190,253,254,255,256,257,300} for 11 fill chars (a A 0 . - _ * space / ~ TAB) = 187 cases.
  C. 43 structural/flag-looking args: '-', '--', '-a', '-h', '--help', '--version', '-V', '--domain=example.com', '.', '..', '...', 'a..b', '-a.com', 'a-.com', 'a b.com', 'a/b.com', '*.com', 'xn--fsq.com', printf-format strings ('%s','%n','%%'), shell-injection shapes ('$PATH','`id`','$(id)'), embedded literal newline/tab/backslash/quote.
  D. Extra trailing arguments beyond the first (must be ignored identically).

Plus 6 explicit boundary spot-checks (len 0/1/63/64/255/256) and the no-argument default path, verified by eyeballing raw od output side by side.

Negative control: re-ran the batch-1 harness with the Rust binary swapped for /bin/echo; it reported 3/3 MISMATCH, confirming the comparator actually detects byte-level, exit-code and stderr differences rather than silently passing.
input.notes:
Zero mismatches. Every case matched byte-for-byte on stdout, both binaries exited 0, and stderr was empty for both in all 2341 invocations.

The sweep was non-degenerate: it exercised all three reachable output classes ("0\n0\n1\n0\n" for empty/over-255, "1\n1\n1\n0\n" for 1..63 bytes, "1\n0\n1\n0\n" for 64..255 bytes). Pure-ASCII input can never produce the IDN class, so the 4th line was correctly "0" throughout — that is expected for this strategy, not a gap in coverage of the ASCII path.

Boundary transitions confirmed identical in both binaries: len 0 -> 0 0 1 0, len 1 -> 1 1 1 0, len 63 -> 1 1 1 0, len 64 -> 1 0 1 0, len 255 -> 1 0 1 0, len 256 -> 0 0 1 0.

Control characters embedded mid-argument (TAB, LF, CR, ESC, 0x01, 0x02, 0x07, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x7F) are accepted by both and counted as ordinary length-contributing bytes; they produced no divergence. Leading-hyphen arguments are not treated as flags by either binary — '--help' prints 1 1 1 0 (6 bytes) from both, so the Rust port's use of std::env::args_os().nth(1) matches the C++ argv[1] semantics with no accidental clap-style parsing.

Extra arguments past the first are ignored identically by both.

Caveats on coverage limits inherent to this strategy: NUL (0x00) cannot be passed through execve argv, so it was untested; bytes above 0x7F were out of scope for the RANDOM ASCII assignment and are covered by other strategies. Within pure ASCII, the established byte-length-only spec held on every single case — no input was found that breaks it.

Source of truth for the C++ side: /workspace/dataset/test4_executable. Rust side: /output/test4 (from /output/test4.rs plus /output/src/idna/{mod,cli,ascii,validate,limits}.rs). Harness scripts left at /tmp/rand_ascii.sh, /tmp/rand2.sh, /tmp/rand3.sh, negative control at /tmp/negctl.sh.
